title: Packing the waste-collection kit before a route
audience: Cleaners who run a waste route in offices, shared buildings and turnover sites.
learningOutcomes: List the core items for a waste-collection kit and state what each item is for.
Pack the kit so that supplies stay within reach during the route.
Check the kit against the site card and act on any shortage before leaving the storage room.

instruction.heading: Why a waste route needs its own kit
instruction.body: A waste route moves from desk to desk, and for much of it you are carrying a full collection bin. A planned kit keeps supplies within reach, so you are not walking back to the storage room for each item. Build the kit before you leave the storage room, and keep it the same for each site so the routine stays predictable.

instruction.heading: The core items
instruction.body: Bring a wheeled collection bin with a tie-off bag and a carry tote for small items. Carry liners in three sizes matched to the bins on the route. Add a dusting cloth, a small brush, a set of cloths for touch points, and a spray bottle of approved sanitiser. Take a plastic drop sheet to lay down where full bags will wait, and a scoop for ash and small debris. Wear the personal protective equipment set for the site, usually eye protection and gloves.

instruction.heading: Keeping the kit within reach
instruction.body: Place the most-used items on top of the tote and the heaviest items low on the bin. Keep small items where your hand reaches without looking. Use a caddy or tote that fits the bin, so your hands stay free for doors and for moving between cubicles.

procedure: Put on the personal protective equipment in the storage room.
Load liners in the three sizes the site card lists.
Add cloths, duster, brush and sanitiser spray to the tote.
Place the drop sheet and scoop in the kit.
Check the kit against the site card before you leave the room.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner is loading a bin for a floor of forty desks and finds only medium liners in stock. The site card lists large liners for the bigger bins.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should happen before the route starts?
workedExamples.reasoning: Check the liner size the site card lists for each bin. Without the large liners, raise a restock request before leaving the storage room. A route started with the wrong liners is harder to finish cleanly, so the kit is checked before the route begins.

equipmentAndPpe: Wheeled collection bin with a tie-off bag
Dusting cloth, small brush and touch-point cloths
Sanitiser spray bottle, labelled and filled

commonErrors.error: Walking back to the storage room for items that were forgotten.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the kit against the list before leaving the room.

commonErrors.error: Starting with the wrong liner sizes for the bins on the route.
commonErrors.prevention: Match the liner sizes to the site card before the first bin.

commonErrors.error: Packing the bin so full that it cannot be lifted safely.
commonErrors.prevention: Load the lightest items first and check the weight at the first bag change.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Inspect the bin and tote for sharp edges, cracks or loose wheels before use.
Do not overload a bin so that it cannot be moved safely by one person.

qualityStandard: The kit matches the site card for bins, liner sizes and supplies.
The sanitiser spray bottle is labelled and filled before the route starts.
documentationEvidence: Kit check noted on the job sheet.
Restock requests logged with the date.
summary: A packed kit keeps supplies within reach and cuts out repeat trips.
Check the liner sizes and supplies against the site card before you leave.
Inspect the bin and tote for damage before use.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why do you pack the waste-collection kit before leaving the storage room?
options: So supplies stay within reach and you avoid repeated trips
So you can start the route before the client arrives
Because the kit replaces the site card

knowledgeChecks.question: The site card calls for large liners, but only medium liners are on hand. What should you do?
options: Use medium liners in the large bins and say nothing to the supervisor
Raise a restock request and do not start the route with the wrong liners
Skip the large bins and mark the route complete and sign the route sheet

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of the kit must be checked for damage before use?
options: The wheeled bin, the tote and any sharp or cracked parts
The client's keyboard and the desk lamp on the shelf
The label on the cleaning bottle only
